Do not weaken this back to "token" - it was written from the wire.

data.name: Cert_ReloadExplanation
data.value: because the proxy is what presents this certificate to printers, and it read the current one when it started. The application itself keeps running. A printer that is already connected keeps meeting the old certificate until it next reconnects, since the reload is graceful and does not interrupt live connections. Nothing is needed at the printers either: both certificates are signed by the authority, which this does not touch.

data.name: Cameras_SourceScheme
data.value: Homespool does not read cameras over {0}. Use rtsp, rtsps, http, https, rtmp or onvif.
data.comment: {0} is the URI scheme as typed. The list of accepted schemes is protocol vocabulary and is not translated.

data.name: Cameras_SourceIsThisServer
data.value: {0} resolves to {1}, which is this server itself rather than a camera on your network.
data.comment: {0} is the host as typed, {1} the address it resolved to.

data.name: Cameras_NotFoundOrNotYours
data.value: That camera does not exist, or is not yours to change.

data.name: Cameras_AttachedNeedsAdministrator
data.value: A camera plugged into this server can only be set up by an administrator. A camera reachable over the network does not need one.

data.name: Cameras_NotYourTeam
data.value: You cannot add a camera to that team.

data.name: Cameras_StreamServerRefused
data.value: Saved, but the go2rtc service would not accept this source. Check the address, and that it is still running.
data.comment: go2rtc is the service's own name and stays as it is.

data.name: Cameras_NoPictureLocal
data.value: Saved, but no picture came back. Check that the go2rtc service in compose.yaml can reach video devices, and that nothing else on this machine is already using it.

data.name: Cameras_NoPictureNetwork
data.value: Saved, but no picture came back yet. If the camera is switched on and reachable, try the page again in a moment - some cameras take a few seconds to answer.

data.name: Bundle_AddressSurvivesLease
data.value: Survives a change of address, but only if your router publishes names to its own DNS. Test it before relying on it.

data.name: Bundle_AddressIsTheContainers
data.value: This looks like a Docker address, which is this container’s own - printers on your network cannot reach it. Use the address of the machine running Docker instead.

data.name: Bundle_AddressUntilLeaseMoves
data.value: Works immediately and needs no DNS, but stops working if this machine’s address changes. A DHCP reservation, or a static address set on the machine itself, stops it changing.
data.comment: Two genuinely different fixes, which the wording used to state as one and a synonym: a "static lease" is another name for a DHCP reservation, not a third option. A static address is set on the machine and does not involve DHCP at all.

data.name: Bundle_AddressUnclassified
data.comment: The Undefined arm. Unreachable in practice - Describe assigns one of the three real values - and present so that adding a durability without adding words for it shows up as a bland line rather than a missing key.

data.name: Queue_HoldInsufficientSpace
data.value: Not enough space on the printer: {0} needs {1} bytes, and {2} are free.
data.comment: {0} is the file name, {1} its size, {2} the free space the printer reported when the queue was held. The numbers are bytes because that is what the printer said - rounding them here would make the two figures stop adding up against what its own screen shows.

data.name: Queue_HoldFileExists
data.value: The printer already has a different file called {0}: {1} bytes there, {2} here. Delete it at the printer, or rename this one.
data.comment: {0} is the file name, {1} the size on the printer, {2} the size here.

data.name: Queue_HoldFileExistsUnknownSize
data.value: The printer already has a file called {0} and would not say how big it is, so it cannot be confirmed as this one. Delete it at the printer, or rename this one.
data.comment: Deliberately not merged with Queue_HoldFileExists: one says the file is demonstrably not ours, this one says it cannot be confirmed either way, and a reader acts differently on each.

data.name: Queue_WaitTransferringUnnamed
data.value: Sending the next file to the printer.
data.comment: A separate key rather than a placeholder filled with a stand-in phrase, so a translator sees the whole sentence.

data.name: Queue_WaitAwaitingPath
data.value: Waiting for the printer to confirm the file's name.

data.name: Queue_WaitPrinterNotReady
data.value: Waiting for the printer to be made ready.
data.comment: States a rule nothing else on the page does - only a person offers a printer up for work - and that rule is what makes a correctly-working queue look broken to somebody who does not know it.

data.name: Ini_HowToLoad
data.value: Homespool provisioning. Copy this file to the root of a USB stick - not into a folder, or the printer will not find it - and load it from the printer's own menu:
data.comment: Ends at the colon. The menu path follows on a line of its own, unwrapped and in English, because it names a menu in the printer's firmware and is the one thing in this comment somebody will hunt for. Same class as the PrusaSlicer paths - see notes/localisation.md.

data.name: Ini_TokenIsAPassword
data.value: This file carries a token that enrols this printer. Treat it as you would a password, and delete it from the stick once the printer has connected.

data.name: Ini_CustomCertNote
data.value: custom_cert = 1 makes connect.der, beside this file, the printer's ENTIRE trust store - replacing the certificates it shipped with rather than adding to them. While that is set, this printer cannot talk to Prusa Connect. Set custom_cert = 0 to undo it.
data.comment: The key names are firmware's and stay as they are. "trust store" stays too - it is the term the firmware documentation uses.

data.name: Ini_PlainHttpNote
data.value: tls = False: this printer's token crosses the network in clear, and so does everything it says afterwards. That is a setting for reading the wire on a network you control.

data.name: Ini_SectionScope
data.value: Only [service::connect] is written here. Your [network] section and wifi credentials are yours - this server has never had them.

data.name: Readme_Title
data.comment: {0} is the printer's name, or Readme_APrinter.

data.name: Readme_Intro
data.value: This zip sets a Prusa printer up to talk to **your** Homespool server instead of Prusa Connect. It was generated for one printer and one server; it is not reusable and not transferable.

data.name: Readme_RowIni
data.value: the settings your printer reads, including a token that enrols it

data.name: Readme_RowDer
data.value: the certificate authority your printer will validate this server's certificate against

data.name: Readme_RowReadme
data.value: this file, which the printer ignores

data.name: Readme_Step1Body
data.value:
Copy the files to the **top level** of the stick - not into a folder. If you end up with a folder on the stick, the printer will not find anything and will not tell you why.
A stick that already works with your printer is the right stick. If you are formatting a new one, use FAT32.

data.name: Readme_Step2Heading
data.value: 2. Put the stick in the printer

data.name: Readme_Step2Body
data.value: Any USB port it normally uses.

data.name: Readme_Step3TlsBody
data.value: `connect.der` is the certificate authority your printer will validate this server's certificate against, and the ini tells it to use that file and nothing else. One without the other does not work: the ini alone leaves the printer with no way to verify the server, and the certificate alone is never read.

data.name: Readme_Step3PlainHeading
data.value: 3. This bundle has no certificate, deliberately

data.name: Readme_Step3PlainBody
data.value: This server is configured to talk to printers over plain HTTP, so there is nothing for the printer to verify and no `connect.der` in the zip. The token below crosses your network in clear text. That is a setting for testing, not for a printer you rely on.

data.name: Readme_Step4Body
data.value: On the printer: **{0}**, or on some firmware simply **{1}**. The printer reads the file, restarts its connection, and within a few seconds should show as online.
data.comment: {0} and {1} are the printer's own menu paths, left in English for the same reason as Ini_HowToLoad.

data.name: Readme_Step5Body
data.value: The printer appears under **{0}** in Homespool. It enrols itself on first contact, so there is nothing else to press.
data.comment: {0} is Homespool's own navigation label and is therefore translated - unlike the printer's menu paths.

data.name: Readme_DeleteHeading
data.value: When it has worked, delete the file

data.name: Readme_DeleteBody
data.value: `prusa_printer_settings.ini` contains a token that is this printer's password to your server. Once the printer has connected, delete it from the stick. Nothing needs it again - the printer has kept what it needs.

data.name: Readme_NoConnectHeading
data.value: While this bundle is loaded, the printer cannot use Prusa Connect

data.name: Readme_NoConnectBody
data.value: `custom_cert = 1` **replaces** the certificates your printer shipped with, rather than adding to them. That is what lets it trust your server, and it is also why it can no longer verify Prusa's. To undo it, load an ini with `custom_cert = 0` and the Prusa Connect settings you want back.

data.name: Readme_TroubleConfigFailed
data.value: **The printer says the config failed to load.** Something edited the file. It is sensitive about comment characters (`#` only, never `;`) and about being complete - every key has to be there. Re-download the bundle rather than repairing it by hand; that is the entire reason it is generated.

data.name: Readme_TroubleTls
data.value: **The printer says there is a TLS or certificate error.** Three usual causes, in order of likelihood: `connect.der` was not copied alongside the ini; the server's certificate has been reissued since this bundle was downloaded, so download a fresh one; or the printer's clock is far enough out to reject the certificate, which fixes itself once it has been on a network with internet access for a minute.

data.name: Readme_TroubleNothing
data.value: **Nothing happens at all.** Check the printer can reach `{0}` on port `{1}` from where it sits - a different wifi network or a firewall between the two is the usual answer.

data.name: Readme_TroubleStopped
data.value: **It worked for weeks and then stopped.** Most likely this server's address changed. Your router hands it out on a lease, and a reboot or a busy network can move it. Give this server a **static lease** - sometimes called a DHCP reservation, or address binding - in your router's settings. It takes a minute and it is the one change that stops this recurring; without it, every move means walking a stick to every printer again.
data.comment: Correctly says a static lease is also called a DHCP reservation. Bundle_AddressUntilLeaseMoves used to offer the two as alternatives, which they are not.

data.name: Readme_TroubleLostDownload
data.value: **You lost the download before the printer connected.** Nothing is broken. In Homespool, use **{0}** on the printer's row and download a new bundle; the old token stops working the moment you do.
data.comment: {0} is Homespool's own button label and is translated with it.

data.name: Readme_ConnectionTls
data.value: TLS - the same encryption your browser calls HTTPS. This is the `tls = True` line in the ini.

data.name: Readme_ConnectionPlain
data.value: plain HTTP, **not encrypted**. This is the `tls = False` line in the ini, and it is for testing only.

data.name: Readme_FileName
data.comment: The name of the file, which is a word rather than a format. Nothing parses it - the printer ignores this file entirely - so unlike prusa_printer_settings.ini and connect.der it is free to be translated. The extension stays, being a format.

data.name: Intent_PausePrint
data.comment: The words for an intent in a status message - "{0} sent." Named for the type so PrinterIntentText can build the key from IPrinterIntent.Name, the way PrinterStatusText builds one from a status. The type name itself is a developer's word and was reaching the page before this existed.
